messages:
Rohit (acme): Hey team — our account (org_id: org_9X4) ran out of monthly credits ~05:30 IST today even though our billing cycle should reset on the 1st at 00:00 local time. Can you confirm when credits actually reload?
Ava (support): sorry you're hitting this, @Rohit. quick check — are you saying the reset was earlier than expected (so gap) or later (so you lost a partial day)? :eyes:
Rohit (acme): earlier. We expected reset at 00:00 Asia/Kolkata on the 1st but credits showed zero at 05:30 IST (so 00:00 UTC +5.5 mismatch). We were doing a large batch job overnight and got 429s.
Ava (support): got it. can you DM me the account id and a request id from one of the 429 responses? we'll pull logs.
Rohit (acme): request id: req_xyz123. sent DM.
OpsBot: New support ticket created — ticket#SUP-4821.
Ava (support): triaging — @Devlin (billing) can you confirm the canonical reset policy? my notes say resets at billing-anchor midnight according to the org's billing timezone if set, otherwise UTC anchored to creation date. but timezone handling has had edgecases.
Devlin (billing): quick summary — two possible systems: (1) public hosted accounts: monthly quotas reset at 00:00 in the org.billing_timezone if that field is set on the org. (2) legacy-accounts or ones that migrated before tz feature: we default to UTC and store anchor_ts in UTC. DST shouldn't affect month boundaries but offset differences between local midnight and UTC can make the apparent reload time earlier/later.
Priya (eng-oncall): adding context — we recently fixed a bug where customers in non-whole-hour offsets (like India +5:30) sometimes saw a half-day shift when their org had an unset billing_timezone and UI displayed local midnight. backend reset runs on UTC midnight anchored to the billing anchor timestamp. That could explain an apparent 5.5h discrepancy.
Ava (support): ok — so likely root cause: org.billing_timezone wasn't set, or anchor stored in UTC. Devlin — can you check org_9X4.billing_timezone and the quota ledger for the last cycle?
Devlin (billing): checking now. pulled the ledger: last reset at 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z, quota_debit events show heavy usage between 2026-03-01T00:30:00Z and 2026-03-01T03:15:00Z (that maps to 05:30–09:15 IST). That aligns with the customer's batch job. org.billing_timezone is null for org_9X4. anchor_ts was set at creation to 2025-03-01T00:00:00Z.
Rohit (acme): so because billing_timezone is null, reset happened at 00:00Z (which is 05:30 IST), and our expectation of 00:00 IST was wrong. ok makes sense but can we avoid outages?
Ava (support): short-term: we can manual-topup for today to cover their batch and avoid repeated 429s. medium-term: advise customer to set billing timezone in org settings to their local tz so resets align to their local midnight. long-term: file infra/console work to show billing timezone in org settings and warn during creation.
Priya (eng-oncall): for reproducibility and to help engineering: steps to repro locally (internal runbook):

1. curl the usage/ledger endpoint (internal API):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" 
  "https://internal.redwood/api/v1/orgs/org_9X4/ledger?start=2026-02-28T00:00:00Z&end=2026-03-02T00:00:00Z"
```

sample response (truncated):
```
{
  "ledger": [
    {"ts":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z","type":"quota_reset","new_balance":1000000},
    {"ts":"2026-03-01T00:30:12Z","type":"quota_use","amount":120000},
    {"ts":"2026-03-01T02:10:05Z","type":"quota_use","amount":300000}
  ]
}
```
2. check org record: `select id, billing_timezone, created_at from orgs where id='org_9X4';`
3. confirm app-facing UI: `GET /v1/orgs/org_9X4` (public API) returns `billing_timezone: null` for this customer.

Priya (eng-oncall): if you want to simulate customer behaviour set your local tz to Asia/Kolkata and run a job that consumes tokens right after UTC midnight to see the apparent early exhaustion.
Devlin (billing): actionables — I'll manually add a transient credit top-up of 48h worth of tokens to org_9X4 (audit record will show admin_manual_topup). doing now. note: manual top-ups are the supported mitigation for immediate outages.
Ava (support): thanks @Devlin. Devlin — can you paste the audit id when done so I can notify Rohit?
Devlin (billing): done — audit id topup_A94F. added +500k tokens, expires 2026-03-03T00:00:00Z. :white_check_mark:
Ava (support): Rohit — I've applied a temporary top-up for today, you should see requests succeed again. I also added a note to the org to set a billing timezone if you want resets at local midnight.
Rohit (acme): saw the green ✅, tests passing now, thank you! Really appreciate the quick turnaround.
Ava (support): follow-ups: (1) please set billing timezone in Console under Org settings if you want local resets; we can set it for you if preferred. (2) we'll file a product ticket to surface billing_timezone on org creation and flag customers with null tz for outreach.
Priya (eng-oncall): product/backlog note: customers with null tz -> documentation + console banner. also consider a lint/check during onboarding.
Devlin (billing): triage complete for this ticket. root cause = org.billing_timezone null -> reset happens at stored UTC anchor (00:00Z) -> customer expected local midnight -> apparent mismatch because Asia/Kolkata = UTC+5:30.
Ava (support): closing loop with customer: "Root cause: billing timezone unset for your org — resets use UTC anchor, causing the reset to occur at 05:30 IST. Resolution: manual top-up applied (audit: topup_A94F). Recommended action: set billing timezone in Org settings to Asia/Kolkata to align future resets to your local midnight — or we can set it for you."
